problem: More than one in five American adults is an unpaid family caregiver. Many do it from far away, piecing care together from pill organizers, sticky notes and group texts.
solution: Hearth turns Alexa+ into the shared memory between a parent and the family looking after her. It's a self-hosted MCP server, built on the latest MCP spec, over Streamable HTTP.
intro: Here it is in a simulated Alexa+ Echo Show. Every call on the right is live MCP traffic to Hearth.
fall: Margaret just talks. When something sounds urgent, Hearth asks before alerting anyone.
elicit: That question comes from inside the tool call, using MCP elicitation.
card: The weekly digest is an MCP App, rendered right on the screen.
arch: Every device and family member shares one household. Hearth is also built for the Alexa+ MCP Toolkit, with OAuth account linking, PKCE, and tool calls under half a second.
probe: We also open-sourced mcp-http-probe, a conformance checker for any Streamable HTTP MCP server. Hearth passes all twenty-three checks. It's on npm and the GitHub Marketplace.
outro: Hearth. One household, every device, and nobody has to remember everything alone.
